summary: Reproduced four failing CPU retraction cases where accepted GDN ReplaySSM ring updates were lost, then fixed both backup routes by materializing the selected request row's pending replay history into its physical checkpoint before the CPU copy.

tests.what_was_measured: Unmodified base: the issue-provided six-case GPU reproducer had four numerical assertion failures (both CPU backup routes with pending=3 and wrapped pending=5/base=14); both no-pending boundaries passed. Raw output: reports/j-e3c8fe329a4c/raw/baseline_reproducer.log

All six cases passed after the fix against an independent float64 sequential recurrence, including both backup routes, wrapped and non-wrapped rings, repeat backup, neighboring-state isolation, KV/conv restoration, and float32/bfloat16 no-pending boundaries. Raw output: reports/j-e3c8fe329a4c/raw/final_regression.log
Five existing ReplaySSM ring allocation/accounting boundary tests passed. Raw output: reports/j-e3c8fe329a4c/raw/ring_accounting.log

gpu_evidence: The regression executed on the assigned GPU 0, reported by rocm-smi as AMD Instinct MI355X with GFX Version gfx950 and Unique ID 0x91222c17f0f648d7. The test performed real device allocation, ReplaySSM Triton materialization, CPU backup, row release/reallocation, restore, and numerical comparison.
remaining_limitations: No Qwen3.5-0.8B weights were available, so the reported full serving-path scenario and semantic output were not reproduced. This validates the exact state-management path with the deterministic GPU fixture only; it does not claim full-model or distributed validation. No native C++/FlyDSL source changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
